ClientResponses.Response:
Hi! Congratulations on your new grill! We are sorry to see some rust spots developing on the side table. If your grill is located in a coastal or humid area, or if chlorine is present in your environment, additional maintenance will be needed to keep up the appearance of the exterior steel parts. Below are a couple helpful tips.
1. At the first sign of staining/discoloration/surface rust we would recommend cleaning with stainless steel cleaner. Once cleaned, we recommend using a stainless steel polish to keep it looking its best in-between cleanings.
2. Once a week we would recommend wiping down the grill with a wet towel or rag and then drying completely.
3. We would only recommend covering your grill if you know inclement weather is coming. 
And please remember, the quicker you get at a stain the easier it will be to clean off.

In regard to the grease dripping from the lid, what you are noticing is actually not uncommon on a new grill. The grease leaking is caused by vapors produced while cooking food, that collects on the interior surfaces of the lid. The interior surfaces on a new grill are so smooth that the vapors collect and run down the surfaces. As the grill is used more, the grease will subside as the lid will not be as smooth any longer. Do not hesitate to reach out to us if you have any questions. Thanks!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber Grills

Results.ReviewText: Got my grill SII-E210.  Put it together in about 2 hours this morning.  It was easy.  HOWEVER:  1.  Read and follow, exactly, precisely, the instructions.  Don't skip ahead, don't think you know how it goes together.  READ and FOLLOW the instructions EXACTLY and all will be well.  2.  The only real dangers are cross-threading one of the multitude of screws or breaking the weld on one of the nuts.  Take your time and get the screws started correctly and use a wrench to hold the nuts as you tighten.  3.  The instructions say to use a soft surface.  Do so.  I laid all the parts out on a rug in the garage and put the hardware in a Plano box (fishing lures box) labeled "A", "B" etc.  The leg pieces are screwed together from the end and side.  Start the end screws first and let them pull the side holes into alignment instead of trying to force and hold it.  The grill fit together correctly, all necessary parts and hardware were in the box, and nothing was damaged out of the box.  Basically an easy assembly - IF you read and follow the instruction.  This is an assembly review only.  I'll report back with cooking results after a few weeks of use.
Results.Title: Assembly

After hooking up the propane, I could not get the grill lite and tried the troubleshooting tips...still with no success.  I called the Help Line and spoke with Laurie and she walked me through getting this grill lite and it was as easy as I had just not tightened the propane nozzle to the grill enough!  WooHoo!  Everything is working and I BBQ bone-in chops.  Still learning, but I'm having fun!  Thanks Laurie!!

44010001.Name: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
44010001.Description:
Open the door to the world of grilling with crazy good food and friends coming together. Equipped with the powerful GS4 grilling system, this two burner gas grill is your entry to the Weber family and to everyday grilling. The compact open-cart design and the practical folding side table makes it fit even on small spaces, and you have all the basics you need to get familiar with gas grilling. So whether it’s a busy Monday or a relaxed Sunday – invite a couple of friends over, push the ignition and enjoy the special atmosphere that surrounds the grill.


 This product requires assembly.
